item.title: Man charged in connection with death of Michael Gaine
item.description: A man's been charged in connection with the death of Michael Gaine. The 56-year-old farmer was reported missing last March. Human tissue found on his farm nearly two months later was confirmed to be his. Advertisement Gardaí yesterday arrested a man in his 50s as part of the investigation. He's been charged and is due before Tralee District Court this afternoon.

item.title: Reviews into failures at Portiuncula close to completion
item.description: Another five reviews into maternity service failures in Portiunclula University Hospital will be completed by the end of next month. It comes after a number of babies, dating back to 2023, were either still-born or born with serious health complications. Seven reviews have already been undertaken by the previous Master of the Rotunda Hospital, bringing the total number of investigations to 12 by the end of March. item.title: Gardaí issue traffic advice ahead of Roscommon v Dublin game
item.description: Gardai in Roscommon have issued traffic advice ahead of the Roscommon v Dublin game this weekend. The game gets underway on Sunday at 2pm at King and Moffatt Dr Hyde Park. In a statement, Gardai say there will be a traffic management plan in place and all motorists can expect delays in and around Roscommon town and the surrounding areas between midday and up to 5pm on Sunday evening. item.title: Bluetongue impacting on trade for local farmers
item.description: The impact over the increasing number of bluetongue outbreaks on local farms has been raised on the floor of the Seanad. Over the last two days, it was detected in a sixth herd in Wexford, while two other cases in Louth and Wicklow were also detected. Bluetongue does not affect human health or food safety; meat and milk are safe to eat. item.title: Large crowds attend local SNA protests
item.description: Large crowds gathered in Roscommon Town and Castlerea this afternoon to protest against proposed SNA cuts despite a Government u-turn on the move this week. There are also protests outside the Dáil at this evening - with simultaneous demonstrations in Limerick, Cork, Galway, Buncrana. The protests were organised following a public backlash to planned SNA cuts in almost 200 schools around the country. item.title: Assaults on HSE staff condemned locally
item.description: Roscommon Hospital Action Committee says the number of local HSE staff assaulted last year is 'staggering'. There were over 1,700 physical, sexual and verbal attacks on healthcare staff in the west and north west in 2025. It's a 9 per cent increase on the previous year.
